notes: Shopify store, direct HTTP access throughout, no WAF. Nav recovered from the same Builder.io CMS feed as the prior Home-Decor pass. Grepped the full nav feed for New Arrivals-family terms (New Arrivals, New In, Just In, Latest, What's New, New This Season, Recently/Newly Added, Collection). Genuine listing found: /collections/all-new-arrivals, linked from every department dropdown across the mega-menu with the identical URL each time (i.e. one listing, repeated link, not multiple listings). No room-specific New Arrivals sub-collections exist anywhere in the nav (unlike Archive Sale, which does have room facets) - single undifferentiated listing only. QTY METHOD: page's embedded analytics blob reports collection_handle:"all-new-arrivals",total_products:50 - discounted as an unreliable app-level cap, since the identical figure 50 is also reported verbatim on two unrelated collections (all-best-sellers, archive-sale). Used exhaustive enumeration of /collections/all-new-arrivals/products.json?limit=250&page=N instead: page 1 returned 78 unique ids (<250, exhaustive) - used 78 as the true qty. 'COLLECTION' PAGES INSPECTED PER BRIEF: found two candidates named as themed collections rather than literally 'New Arrivals' - 'The Fall 2025 Collection' (/collections/the-fall-2025-collection) and 'The Dunes Collection' (/collections/the-dunes-collection). Both use the site's standard collection/PLP template (filterable product grid, own products.json feed), so both are real listings, not marketing/lookbook pages - but neither carries a New Arrivals signal word (no 'new'/'latest'/'just in' in the name), and both read as themed capsule/product-line collections. Checked whether they are in substance 'the newest additions' by measuring product-id overlap against all-new-arrivals: The Fall 2025 Collection (45 products) has only 22/45 (49%) overlap with New Arrivals - roughly half its catalog is not currently new, so it reads as a broader seasonal aesthetic bundle (mixing new and older pieces), not a recently-added listing - excluded. The Dunes Collection (6 products) is 6/6 (100%) contained within New Arrivals, but it is a themed teak outdoor-furniture product line page (meta description: "Organic form. Effortless comfort. Crafted with sustainably sourced teak to live beautifully outdoors." - pure product description, no newness language) - its full containment in New Arrivals is treated as ordinary category/New-Arrivals overlap (explicitly expected and not an error per the brief), not evidence that the page itself is a New Arrivals PLP - excluded. Neither is recorded as a row (not even flagged ambiguous): for Fall 2025 the ~half-old-catalog composition is clear-cut evidence against 'recently added'; for Dunes there is no New-Arrivals-taxonomy signal on the page at all, only a themed product-line description. Also checked and excluded as non-New-Arrivals: 'Ready to Ship' (/collections/ready-to-ship) and 'Back in Stock' (/collections/all-back-in-stock) - both are genuine site-defined merchandising concepts, but neither means 'newly added to catalogue' (ready-to-ship = fast fulfillment availability; back-in-stock = restocked existing SKUs), so both are out of scope for this brief.

rows.evidence: Exhaustive enumeration of https://www.the-citizenry.com/collections/all-new-arrivals/products.json?limit=250&page=1 returned 78 unique product ids on page 1 (< limit of 250, confirming exhaustive/no further pages). Page's own embedded analytics blob shows collection_handle:"all-new-arrivals",total_products:50, but that figure is discounted as an unreliable app-level cap (identical 50 also appears on two unrelated collections).
